text:
Burj Khalifa (828 m) sits on loose sand and weak sandstone, with salty groundwater 2.5 m below ground. There is no bedrock to reach.

The answer was friction, not rock: 192 bored concrete piles, 1.5 m in diameter and about 50 m deep, under a 3.7 m thick raft, with cathodic protection against the salt.

Why it matters: foundation design follows the ground, not the height. The site's soil report shapes cost, depth and durability long before the first floor goes up.

Source: Bunce and Poulos foundation design (via GeoPrac), Arabian Business. Educational content, not advice.
